title: Where and when: postpositions
intro: Where English puts a preposition before a noun, Turkmen puts a postposition after it: *Aýna bilen*, with Aýna; *agşama çenli*, until the evening; *işden soň*, after work. Each postposition wants its noun in a particular case, so this unit sorts them by case. For positions, Turkmen uses nouns like *üst*, top, and *öň*, front, with **its** and a case ending: *stoluň üstünde*, on the table; *öýüň öňünde*, in front of the house.

sections.title: With, for, like, about: bilen, üçin, ýaly, barada, hakda

blocks.text: These postpositions take a noun as it is, with no case ending, and they are written as separate words. You know three of them: *bilen*, with ([A1 unit 12](a1-u12)); *üçin*, for; *ýaly*, like ([A2 unit 8](a2-u08)). Two new ones both mean **about**: *barada* and *hakda*. *Bu kitap Magtymguly barada*, this book is about Magtymguly; *Näme hakda gürleýärsiňiz?*, what are you talking about?

**With a personal pronoun**, they take the genitive: *meniň bilen*, with me; *seniň üçin*, for you; *onuň ýaly*, like him; *biziň barada*, about us; *seniň hakda*, about you. With *olar* you will mostly hear the plain form: *olar bilen*, *olar üçin*.

items.en: This book is about Magtymguly.
She asked about you.

What is this film about?

blocks.title: Not about me: the genitive
blocks.text: With a pronoun, use the genitive: *meniň barada*, about me, not `men barada` or `maňa barada`. A noun stays as it is: *Aýna barada*, not `Aýnanyň barada`.

sections.title: Until, according to, towards, against, near: the dative

blocks.text: Five postpositions take the dative, `-A`. *çenli*, **until, as far as**, you know from [A1 unit 7](a1-u07): *agşama çenli*, until the evening; *Aşgabada çenli*, as far as Ashgabat. The others:

blocks.caption: Postpositions with the dative
head: Postposition
Meaning
Example
rows: *maňa görä*, in my opinion; *düzgüne görä*, according to the rules

blocks.text: *tarap* is also a noun, **side, direction**: *Mekdep haýsy tarapda?*, which way is the school? After a dative it means **towards**: *Olar şähere tarap gitdiler*, they went towards the town. *ýakyn* you met in [A1 unit 7](a1-u07) as **near**, with the place you start from in the ablative: *bu ýerden ýakyn*, near (from) here. To say what something is close **to**, use the dative: *Mekdep öýümize ýakyn*, the school is close to our house.

items.en: In my opinion, this film is interesting.
They went towards home.
I'm against this plan.
The school is close to our house.
I work until the evening.

blocks.title: In my opinion
blocks.text: *Maňa görä* is the everyday way to give your view: **as far as I'm concerned, I think**. Ask for someone else's with *Size görä?* or *Saňa görä?*, what do you think?

sections.title: After, before, since, apart from: the ablative

blocks.text: Four take the ablative, `-dAn`. You know two from earlier units: *soň*, **after** (*işden soň*, after work) and *öň*, **before** (*nahardan öň*, before the meal). The new ones are *bäri*, **since**, and *başga*, **apart from, except**.

*bäri* counts from a point in time up to now: *irden bäri*, since the morning; *2020-nji ýyldan bäri*, since 2020; *köp ýyldan bäri*, for many years. Where English says **I have lived** or **I have been waiting**, Turkmen uses the present, because it is still going on: *Men 2020-nji ýyldan bäri Aşgabatda ýaşaýaryn*, I have lived in Ashgabat since 2020. Ask with *Haçandan bäri?*, since when?

*başga*, which you know as **other** ([A1 unit 10](a1-u10)), means **apart from, except** after the ablative: *senden başga*, apart from you. It goes well with the negative words of [A2 unit 5](a2-u05): *Senden başga hiç kim bilmeýär*, nobody knows apart from you.

items.en: I've been waiting since the morning.
I've lived in Ashgabat since 2020.
Wash your hands before the meal!
What would you like apart from tea?
Everyone came except Aýna.

blocks.title: Since needs the present
blocks.text: *Irden bäri garaşýaryn*, not `garaşdym`: the waiting hasn't stopped. And *bäri* needs the ablative: *ýyldan bäri*, not `ýylda bäri`.

sections.title: On, under, in front, behind: place nouns

blocks.text: For positions Turkmen uses nouns: *üst*, the top; *aşak*, the underside; *öň*, the front; *yz*, the back; *gapdal* and *ýan*, the side; *iç*, the inside; *daş*, the outside; *ara*, the space between. To say **on the table**, say **in the table's top**: the thing in the genitive, the place noun with **its**, the *n* of [A1 unit 10](a1-u10), and the locative.

blocks.caption: Where: the locative
head: Place noun
Where
Meaning
rows: in the bag, inside the bag

blocks.text: **The spelling** follows rules you know. After a rounded first syllable the vowel rounds: *üstünde*, *öňünde*. A final *k* becomes *g*: *aşagynda*. After a vowel, **its** is *-sY*: *arasynda*. And the *n* always comes before the case: *üstünde*, never `üstüde`. The loanword *stol* rounds too: *stoluň*; you will also see *stolyň*.

**Change the case** to say where to or where from: the dative for movement towards, the ablative for movement away. *Kitaby stoluň üstüne goý*, put the book on the table; *Ol sumkanyň içinden telefon çykardy*, she took a phone out of the bag; *Pişik ýatagyň aşagyndan çykdy*, the cat came out from under the bed.

blocks.caption: Three cases on üst
head: Case
Form
Meaning
rows: off the table, from on the table

blocks.text: **With a pronoun**, the possessive changes to match: *meniň ýanymda*, next to me; *seniň öňüňde*, in front of you; *biziň aramyzda*, between us. The genitive pronoun can drop, as with any possessive: *Ýanyma gel!*, come over to me!

blocks.title: *ýan*: next to me, next to you…

blocks.text: *ýan* is also **someone's place**: *Men Merdanyň ýanyna barýaryn*, I'm going to see Merdan. For **between two things**, join them with *bilen* and put the genitive on the second: *mekdep bilen bazaryň arasynda*, between the school and the market.

items.en: The cat is under the bed.
The car is behind the house.
The shop is next to the school.
Put the book on the table.
I'm going to see Merdan.
The stop is between the post office and the market.

blocks.title: Two small words, one big idea
blocks.text: English needs **on**, **onto** and **off** for three ideas. Turkmen keeps one place noun, *üst*, and changes the case: *üstünde*, *üstüne*, *üstünden*. Learn the noun once, then add the case you need.

summary: *bilen*, *üçin*, *ýaly*, *barada*, *hakda* (about) take a noun as it is and a pronoun in the genitive: *Aýna barada*, *seniň hakda*.
*çenli*, *görä*, *tarap*, *garşy*, *ýakyn* take the dative: *agşama çenli*, *maňa görä*, *öýe tarap*, *oňa garşy*, *öýe ýakyn*.
*soň*, *öň*, *bäri*, *başga* take the ablative: *işden soň*, *nahardan öň*, *irden bäri*, *senden başga*.
With *bäri*, an action still going on is in the present: *2020-nji ýyldan bäri Aşgabatda ýaşaýaryn*.
Positions: genitive + place noun + **its** + *n* + case: *stoluň üstünde*, *öýüň öňünde*, *ýatagyň aşagynda*.
Dative for **to**, ablative for **from**: *üstüne*, *içinden*; with pronouns, *ýanymda*, *öňüňde*; *Merdanyň ýanyna*, to see Merdan.
